requirements.exact_constitution_section: AI Master Instruction and Primary Objective
requirements.source_wording: AI MASTER INSTRUCTION / You are NOT a coding assistant. / You are an elite team of professionals working together as one AI. / You must simultaneously think and work as: / CEO / CTO / Product Owner / Business Consultant / Product Strategist / Startup Advisor / SaaS Architect / Senior Software Architect / Senior PHP/Laravel Engineer (or recommend a better stack if justified) / Database Architect / Cloud Infrastructure Engineer / DevOps Engineer / Security Engineer / QA Engineer / Performance Engineer / UI Designer / UX Researcher / SEO Expert / Digital Marketing Strategist / Content Marketing Expert / Technical Writer / Documentation Specialist / System Analyst / Do not immediately begin writing code.
requirements.source_summary: The delivery agent operates as a multidisciplinary product, engineering, security, operations, design, marketing, QA, and documentation organization rather than immediately acting as a coding assistant.
requirements.atomic_acceptance_criteria: Workflow and audit evidence confirm this statement: “The delivery agent operates as a multidisciplinary product, engineering, security, operations, design, marketing, QA, and documentation organization rather than immediately acting as a coding assistant.”
requirements.evidence_requirement: Approval/audit record showing the required gate or workflow was followed.

ODR.label: ODR
ODR.title: Authoritative Phase 0 document map
ODR.description: The Constitution names many required deliverables but does not assign the EP-P0-02 through EP-P0-13 identifiers or ownership map.
ODR.source_excerpt: No Constitution wording is claimed for this gap.
ODR.decision_or_evidence_needed: Approve the definitive Phase 0 document list, IDs, titles, owners, and requirement-to-document mapping.

ODR.label: ODR
ODR.title: Backend technology and runtime architecture
ODR.description: Select the backend framework/runtime and migration path after the mandated comparison.
ODR.source_excerpt: BACKEND ARCHITECTURE / Do not assume a fixed backend technology. / Evaluate suitable technologies based on: / Free-tier friendliness / Scalability / Security / Maintainability / Performance / Developer productivity / Long-term sustainability / Compare appropriate options (such as PHP frameworks, serverless platforms, managed databases, and supporting services) and recommend the best architecture with clear reasoning. / The recommendation should prioritize a smooth migration path from free infrastructure to paid infrastructure as the platform grows. || BACKEND INFRASTRUCTURE / The AI must evaluate backend options based on: / Performance / Security / Cost / Developer availability / Maintenance requirements / Possible options may include: / PHP/Laravel / Node.js / Serverless Functions / Other modern backend approaches / The final recommendation must include: / Why selected / Why alternatives rejected / Scaling path
ODR.decision_or_evidence_needed: Approve the backend stack, deployment model, scaling path, and rejected alternatives.

ODR.label: ODR
ODR.title: Launch-country and eligibility matrix
ODR.description: “Other selected European countries” is undefined and country eligibility controls require an authoritative launch matrix.
ODR.source_excerpt: TARGET COUNTRIES / Primary launch markets include: / United States / United Kingdom / Canada / Ireland / Australia / Germany / Belgium / Other selected European countries / Saudi Arabia / United Arab Emirates / Qatar / Oman / Bahrain / The initial public launch should not target Pakistan, India, Bangladesh, or China. / The platform architecture should still be capable of supporting additional countries in the future if the business expands. || The following should be configurable from the admin panel whenever appropriate: / Points-to-USD conversion / Minimum withdrawal amount / Available withdrawal methods / Leaderboard settings / Registration controls / Email templates / Platform announcements / Maintenance mode / Feature flags / Currency display preferences / Country availability
ODR.decision_or_evidence_needed: Approve exact countries, excluded regions, eligibility rules, geolocation policy, and future activation process.

ODR.label: ODR
ODR.title: Frontend architecture and design approvals
ODR.description: Frontend architecture, palette, design system, and implementation approval remain frontend-owner decisions.
ODR.source_excerpt: FRONTEND ARCHITECTURE / The frontend should be: / Responsive / Modular / Accessible / Component-based where appropriate / Optimized for performance / Easy to maintain / The AI should recommend an architecture that balances simplicity with long-term maintainability. || COLOR SYSTEM / The AI should recommend a professional color palette. / Suggested direction: / Primary Color / Deep Blue / Secondary / Emerald Green / Success / Green / Warning / Amber / Danger / Red / Neutral / White / Light Gray / Dark Gray / Avoid using too many colors. || FINAL UI DELIVERABLES / Generate: / Complete Design System / Component Library / Design Tokens / Typography Guide / Color Guide / Responsive Guidelines / Accessibility Review / UX Documentation / Wireframes / High-Fidelity Mockups / Design QA Checklist / Only after approval should UI implementation begin.
ODR.decision_or_evidence_needed: Approve frontend stack, design tokens, accessibility target, responsive baseline, and UI gate.

ODR.label: ODR
ODR.title: V1 withdrawal methods
ODR.description: The architecture should support PayPal, Virtual Visa, and cryptocurrency, but the Constitution does not approve which methods launch in V1.
ODR.source_excerpt: WITHDRAWAL SYSTEM / The withdrawal experience should feel professional and transparent. / Supported withdrawal methods should be designed to support: / PayPal / Virtual Visa / Cryptocurrency / The system architecture should make it easy to add additional methods later. || The following should be configurable from the admin panel whenever appropriate: / Points-to-USD conversion / Minimum withdrawal amount / Available withdrawal methods
ODR.decision_or_evidence_needed: Approve V1 payment methods, country coverage, fees, reserves, settlement flow, and fallback behavior.

ODR.label: ODR
ODR.title: Withdrawal thresholds, fees, and limits
ODR.description: Minimum withdrawal is configurable, but no default threshold, fee, frequency, or account limit is specified.
ODR.source_excerpt: SYSTEM SETTINGS / Avoid hardcoding business values. / The following should be configurable from the admin panel whenever appropriate: / Points-to-USD conversion / Minimum withdrawal amount / Available withdrawal methods || BUSINESS RULE CONFIGURATION / Important business values must be configurable. / Examples: / 1000 Points \= 1 USD / Withdrawal threshold / Available countries / Reward rules / Feature availability / Leaderboard settings / Do not hardcode values that may change.
ODR.decision_or_evidence_needed: Approve threshold, fees, daily/monthly limits, cooldowns, and change-governance policy.

ODR.label: ODR
ODR.title: Sensitive-action verification and KYC trigger policy
ODR.description: Phone OTP is optional for sensitive actions and the OTP channel must be recommended, but the triggering actions and KYC relationship are not decided.
ODR.source_excerpt: Phone verification is not required during registration. / Phone OTP verification should occur only when required for sensitive actions (such as the first withdrawal), if the business chooses to enable it. || OTP INFRASTRUCTURE / OTP requirements: / Secure generation / Expiration / Rate limiting / Abuse prevention / Logging / The AI should recommend: / Email OTP / SMS OTP / Third-party verification services / based on: / Cost / Reliability / Target countries
ODR.decision_or_evidence_needed: Approve sensitive actions, first-withdrawal controls, OTP channel hierarchy, recovery flow, and any KYC triggers.

ODR.label: ODR
ODR.title: Infrastructure platform selection
ODR.description: The Constitution mandates evaluation but does not select the cloud, serverless, managed-service, or hybrid combination.
ODR.source_excerpt: INFRASTRUCTURE STRATEGY / The AI must evaluate available infrastructure options objectively. / Do not select technology based only on popularity. / Evaluate based on: / Free-tier availability / Resource limits / Scalability / Reliability / Security / Developer experience / Documentation quality / Long-term cost / Migration difficulty / \--- / FREE-FIRST APPROACH / During the initial startup phase, prioritize free or extremely low-cost solutions where practical. / The AI should analyze options such as: / AWS Free Tier / AWS Lambda / Cloudflare Workers / Cloudflare Pages / Google Cloud Free Tier / Google Apps Script (where appropriate) / Supabase / Neon PostgreSQL / Managed MySQL/MariaDB solutions / Other suitable startup platforms / The AI must recommend the best combination with reasoning. / Do not choose free services if they create future technical debt.
ODR.decision_or_evidence_needed: Approve hosting providers, regions, service boundaries, migration triggers, and operational ownership.

ODR.label: ODR
ODR.title: Database engine and service
ODR.description: PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, serverless, and managed options must be evaluated before a final engine/service is selected.
ODR.source_excerpt: DATABASE INFRASTRUCTURE / The AI should evaluate: / PostgreSQL / MySQL / MariaDB / Serverless databases / Managed database services / Consider: / Free tier limits / Backups / Performance / Scaling options / Security / Migration possibilities / The database must not become the first bottleneck.
ODR.decision_or_evidence_needed: Approve engine, provider, region, availability model, connection strategy, and scaling triggers.

ODR.label: ODR
ODR.title: Object storage and CDN design
ODR.description: The storage strategy must be defined, but provider, region, retention classes, malware handling, and CDN policy are open.
ODR.source_excerpt: STORAGE ARCHITECTURE / Define storage strategy for: / User uploads / Blog images / Documents / System files / Backups / The AI should consider: / Object storage / CDN integration / Cost optimization
ODR.decision_or_evidence_needed: Approve storage provider, buckets/classes, CDN, upload limits, malware scanning, encryption, and lifecycle rules.

ODR.label: ODR
ODR.title: Backup schedule and storage policy
ODR.description: The backup plan must define frequency and location, but the values are not supplied.
ODR.source_excerpt: BACKUP STRATEGY / Create a complete backup plan. / Include: / Database backups / File backups / Configuration backups / Define: / Backup frequency / Storage location / Recovery process / Testing procedure
ODR.decision_or_evidence_needed: Approve backup frequency, retention, immutability, encryption, geographic placement, and restore-test cadence.

ODR.label: ODR
ODR.title: Recovery objectives
ODR.description: The disaster-recovery strategy must define RTO and RPO, but the targets are not supplied.
ODR.source_excerpt: DISASTER RECOVERY / Create a recovery strategy. / Define: / Recovery Time Objective (RTO) / Recovery Point Objective (RPO) / Emergency procedures / Responsible roles
ODR.decision_or_evidence_needed: Approve RTO/RPO by service tier, incident authority, communications, and exercise cadence.

ODR.label: ODR
ODR.title: Admin roles, permissions, and Limit Template catalog
ODR.description: Role and restriction examples are not a final permission matrix or V1 template catalog.
ODR.source_excerpt: LIMIT TEMPLATE SYSTEM / Instead of manually configuring restrictions every time, create reusable Limit Templates. / Examples: / Template A / Withdrawal Restricted / Template B / Support Only / Template C / Read Only / Template D / Temporary Restriction / Template E / Survey Access Disabled / Each template should allow granular control over platform capabilities. / Examples of configurable permissions include: / Login / Profile Editing / Email Change / Password Change / Survey Access / Wallet Access / Withdrawal Access / Notifications / Blog Access / Referral Module (future) / Promotional Features (future) / Support Ticket Creation / Templates should be editable, cloneable, and assignable to users. / \--- / ROLE MANAGEMENT / The system should support multiple administrator roles. / Examples: / Super Admin / Operations Admin / Finance Admin / Support Admin / Content Admin / Marketing Admin / Developer / Read Only Auditor / Every role should use Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) with granular permissions.
ODR.decision_or_evidence_needed: Approve V1 admin roles, least-privilege matrix, segregation of duties, templates, override rules, expiry, and emergency access.

ODR.label: ODR
ODR.title: Provider launch and visibility policy
ODR.description: The modular framework is required, but provider selection, naming/visibility, per-provider caps, routing, and failure policy are not specified.
ODR.source_excerpt: SURVEY EXPERIENCE / Survey discovery must be extremely simple. / Users should instantly understand: / Reward / Estimated Time / Difficulty (if available) / Availability / Category / Country Eligibility / Device Compatibility / When a survey is clicked: / Open according to provider integration requirements. / Do not modify provider workflows in ways that violate provider agreements. / After completion: / Automatically synchronize status if supported. / If immediate confirmation is unavailable, clearly explain that validation may take time depending on the provider. || PROVIDER INTEGRATION FRAMEWORK / The platform must use a modular provider architecture. / Every provider should behave like a plugin. / Adding or removing a provider should require minimal changes. / The system should abstract provider-specific logic behind a common interface where feasible. / The platform should support independent provider configuration, health monitoring, logging, and error reporting. / Provider integrations must comply with each provider's published requirements and agreements. / \--- / API MANAGEMENT / The admin should be able to: / View API status / Enable or disable integrations / View synchronization logs / Monitor failures / Retry synchronization jobs / View response times / Receive alerts on repeated failures || PROVIDER INTEGRATION LAYER / Create an abstraction layer for external providers. / The AI should design a provider interface that minimizes provider-specific code throughout the application. / When adding a new provider, implementation should primarily involve creating a new integration module rather than modifying core business logic. / Integrations should comply with each provider's published requirements and agreements.
ODR.decision_or_evidence_needed: Approve launch providers, user-facing visibility, routing/caps, credentials ownership, sandbox certification, and disablement criteria.

ODR.label: ODR
ODR.title: Data-retention schedule
ODR.description: Retention policies are required but no durations, legal holds, deletion windows, or anonymization rules are specified.
ODR.source_excerpt: DATA RETENTION / The AI should recommend retention policies for different categories of data. / Examples: / Logs / Audit records / Notifications / Sessions / Support tickets / The recommendations should balance operational needs, storage costs, and applicable legal obligations.
ODR.decision_or_evidence_needed: Approve category-by-category retention, legal hold, deletion/anonymization, backup expiry, and exception workflow.

ODR.label: ODR
ODR.title: Provider-specific maturity and cleared-funds rules
ODR.description: The Constitution defines lifecycle stages and estimated maturity display but not the provider-specific settlement, risk, or cleared-funds policy.
ODR.source_excerpt: BALANCE MATURITY SYSTEM / One of the most important features. / Every earning should have a lifecycle. / Example: / Survey Completed / ↓ / Pending / ↓ / Validated / ↓ / Mature / ↓ / Withdrawable / ↓ / Paid / Every transaction must show: / Status / Provider / Earned Date / Estimated Maturity Date / Amount / Points / USD / Notes / The user should never need to contact support to understand their balance. || Survey Domain / Design the schema to support multiple providers through a common abstraction. / Track information such as: / Survey availability / User participation / Status / Reward / Completion timestamps / Validation status / The exact implementation should respect provider requirements.
ODR.decision_or_evidence_needed: Approve each provider’s validation evidence, maturity conditions, reversal rules, cleared-funds gate, risk holds, and user messaging. Do not adopt a global time-only validation rule.

ODR.label: ODR
ODR.title: Local-currency conversion display
ODR.description: Local currency is display-only, but the exchange-rate source, refresh cadence, rounding, stale-rate policy, and disclaimer are undefined.
ODR.source_excerpt: Users should see: / Points / USD / Estimated Local Currency / Local currency is display-only. / All calculations, accounting, wallet balances, provider earnings, and business reporting must use USD as the source of truth. || Every page should display: / Points / USD / Estimated Local Currency
ODR.decision_or_evidence_needed: Approve authoritative rate source, cadence, snapshot/rounding rules, supported currencies, and disclaimer.

ODR.label: ODR
ODR.title: Reward economics and platform-margin policy
ODR.description: The platform must track provider revenue, user rewards, and margin, while reward rules are configurable; the split and accounting policy are not stated.
ODR.source_excerpt: Revenue / Provider revenue / User rewards / Platform margin || BUSINESS RULE CONFIGURATION / Important business values must be configurable. / Examples: / 1000 Points \= 1 USD / Withdrawal threshold / Available countries / Reward rules / Feature availability
ODR.decision_or_evidence_needed: Approve provider-to-user reward calculation, margin, rounding, promotional funding, negative adjustments, and disclosure policy.

ODR.label: ODR
ODR.title: Age, residency, KYC, and eligibility policy
ODR.description: The Constitution does not define minimum age, residency proof, duplicate-person rules, sanctions screening, KYC thresholds, or restricted-person policy.
ODR.source_excerpt: No Constitution wording is claimed for this gap.
ODR.decision_or_evidence_needed: Approve age/residency eligibility, identity/KYC triggers, duplicate-account rules, sanctions/AML applicability, and country-specific exceptions.

ODR.label: ODR
ODR.title: Manual wallet adjustment governance
ODR.description: The API scope includes wallet adjustments and the ledger must trace financial changes, but maker-checker, reason codes, limits, and reversal policy are open.
ODR.source_excerpt: Transaction history / Adjustment history / All financial changes should be traceable through transactions rather than by directly editing balances. || ADMIN APIs / Design secure administrative APIs for: / User Management / Platform Settings / Wallet Adjustments / Withdrawal Management / CMS Management / Analytics / Audit Logs / Notifications / Moderation / Administrative operations should require appropriate permissions.
ODR.decision_or_evidence_needed: Approve adjustment permissions, dual control, reason/evidence fields, thresholds, reversals, and user notification.

ODR.label: ODR
ODR.title: Support service levels
ODR.description: Support response time is measured and estimated response time is displayed, but no SLA or escalation targets are defined.
ODR.source_excerpt: Withdrawal Request Rate / Support Response Time / User Retention || SUPPORT EXPERIENCE / Support should feel conversational. / Include: / Knowledge Base / Search / Support Tickets / Ticket Timeline / Attachments / Status Updates / Estimated Response Time
ODR.decision_or_evidence_needed: Approve response/resolution targets by priority, business hours, escalation, pause conditions, and disclosure wording.

ODR.label: ODR
ODR.title: Marketing consent and communication preferences
ODR.description: Marketing and retention email capabilities are required, but consent, suppression, frequency, and preference policy are not defined.
ODR.source_excerpt: EMAIL MARKETING SYSTEM / Create an email marketing framework. / Include: / Registration Emails / Welcome email / Verification email / Engagement Emails / New surveys available / Platform updates / Reward reminders / Trust Emails / Security notifications / Account activity / Retention Emails / Inactive user campaigns / Personalized recommendations || Use email infrastructure for: / Account verification / Password reset / Security notifications / Withdrawal notifications / Support updates / Marketing communication (future)
ODR.decision_or_evidence_needed: Approve consent basis, opt-in/out, suppression, frequency caps, quiet hours, and country-specific marketing rules.

ODR.label: ODR
ODR.title: Audit and financial-history retention/immutability
ODR.description: Audit and withdrawal histories should be immutable, but storage guarantees, retention, corrections, and privileged access are not specified.
ODR.source_excerpt: Administrative actions / The history should be immutable wherever practical. || Audit Domain / Maintain immutable records of significant administrative and system actions. / Examples include: / Settings changes / User moderation / Permission changes / Administrative actions || AUDIT LOGGING / Every important administrative action should be logged. / Examples: / User modifications / Permission changes / Withdrawal approvals / Settings changes / Content updates / Login attempts / Failed authentication events / Audit logs should include: / Timestamp / Administrator / Action / Target / Reason (where applicable) / IP information if appropriate / Outcome / Audit records should be searchable.
ODR.decision_or_evidence_needed: Approve append-only guarantees, correction model, retention, access, export, integrity verification, and legal-hold handling.

ODR.label: ODR
ODR.title: Session, rate-limit, and abuse thresholds
ODR.description: Secure sessions, rate limiting, brute-force protection, OTP limiting, and abuse detection are required but numeric policies are absent.
ODR.source_excerpt: The AI must propose a comprehensive security architecture that includes: / Secure authentication / Session management / CSRF protection / XSS protection / SQL injection prevention / Secure password hashing / Rate limiting / Brute-force protection / Input validation / Output encoding / Secure file handling / Secure API design / Security headers / Logging and monitoring || API SECURITY / The API architecture should include recommendations for: / Authentication / Authorization / Rate limiting / Input validation / Output encoding / Request logging / Abuse detection / Session security / Secret management || OTP INFRASTRUCTURE / OTP requirements: / Secure generation / Expiration / Rate limiting / Abuse prevention / Logging
ODR.decision_or_evidence_needed: Approve session lifetimes, refresh/revocation, login/OTP/API thresholds, lockout behavior, exceptions, and monitoring alerts.

ODR.label: ODR
ODR.title: Account deletion, restoration, and anonymization
ODR.description: Soft deletion and restoration are required, but retention, anonymization, owner access, and irreversible deletion rules are not defined.
ODR.source_excerpt: Lock account / Unlock account / Delete account (soft delete) / Restore account || Only collect data that is necessary for the platform.
ODR.decision_or_evidence_needed: Approve soft-delete duration, restoration authority, anonymization/deletion workflow, financial/audit exceptions, and user notices.

ODR.label: ODR
ODR.title: Leaderboard privacy and competition rules
ODR.description: Ranking methods and hidden-user controls are configurable, but opt-out, pseudonyms, ties, anti-gaming, prizes, and dispute rules are not defined.
ODR.source_excerpt: LEADERBOARD SYSTEM / Implement a weekly leaderboard. / Leaderboard should encourage healthy competition. / Possible rankings: / Top Weekly Earners / Top Monthly Earners / Most Surveys Completed / Highest Streak / Highest Referral Count (future feature) / The Super Admin must be able to: / Enable or disable leaderboards. / Reset periods. / Choose ranking methods. / Hide specific users if required. / Create seasonal competitions. / The architecture should support future gamification. || LEADERBOARD EXPERIENCE / Weekly leaderboard should include: / Rank / Display Name / Points Earned / Surveys Completed / Achievement Badges (future) / The design should encourage participation without promoting unhealthy competition.
ODR.decision_or_evidence_needed: Approve privacy/opt-out, display-name rules, rank calculations, ties, exclusions, anti-fraud, seasonal prizes, and disputes.

ODR.label: ODR
ODR.title: Provider reconciliation fallback
ODR.description: Status synchronization is required when supported, but the verified reconciliation process when provider callbacks are absent or disputed is undefined.
ODR.source_excerpt: When a survey is clicked: / Open according to provider integration requirements. / Do not modify provider workflows in ways that violate provider agreements. / After completion: / Automatically synchronize status if supported. / If immediate confirmation is unavailable, clearly explain that validation may take time depending on the provider. || API MANAGEMENT / The admin should be able to: / View API status / Enable or disable integrations / View synchronization logs / Monitor failures / Retry synchronization jobs / View response times / Receive alerts on repeated failures || WEBHOOK ARCHITECTURE / Where supported by providers, design a secure webhook handling system. / Requirements include: / Verification of incoming requests / Logging / Retry handling / Idempotency / Error reporting / Monitoring / Webhook processing should be resilient and auditable.
ODR.decision_or_evidence_needed: Approve polling/import/manual-evidence methods, matching keys, conflict rules, operator permissions, and audit evidence.

DDR.label: DERIVED PROPOSAL — REQUIRES ARCHITECTURE OR OWNER APPROVAL
DDR.title: Immutable reward-lot ledger
DDR.description: Model each earning as an immutable reward lot with append-only ledger postings and derived balance buckets rather than mutable aggregate balances.
DDR.source_excerpt: WALLET SYSTEM / Design a professional wallet similar to fintech applications. / Wallet must include: / Current Balance / Pending Balance / Validated Balance / Mature Balance / Withdrawable Balance / Total Earnings / Total Withdrawals / Processing Withdrawals / Rejected Withdrawals / Reward Points / USD Value / Estimated Local Currency / Wallet History / Transaction History / Provider History / Withdrawal History / Reward History || Wallet Domain / Support: / Reward Points / USD balances / Pending balances / Validated balances / Mature balances / Withdrawable balances / Transaction history / Adjustment history / All financial changes should be traceable through transactions rather than by directly editing balances.
DDR.decision_or_evidence_needed: Architecture review, accounting invariants, reversal model, and performance proof.

DDR.label: DERIVED PROPOSAL — REQUIRES ARCHITECTURE OR OWNER APPROVAL
DDR.title: Event-driven earning state machine
DDR.description: Use an explicit state machine for Pending, Validated, Mature, Withdrawable, Paid, Reversed, and exceptional states, with guarded transitions and recorded causes.
DDR.source_excerpt: BALANCE MATURITY SYSTEM / One of the most important features. / Every earning should have a lifecycle. / Example: / Survey Completed / ↓ / Pending / ↓ / Validated / ↓ / Mature / ↓ / Withdrawable / ↓ / Paid / Every transaction must show: / Status / Provider / Earned Date / Estimated Maturity Date / Amount / Points / USD / Notes || Survey Domain / Design the schema to support multiple providers through a common abstraction. / Track information such as: / Survey availability / User participation / Status / Reward / Completion timestamps / Validation status / The exact implementation should respect provider requirements.
DDR.decision_or_evidence_needed: Owner approval of transition matrix and provider-specific rules.

DDR.label: DERIVED PROPOSAL — REQUIRES ARCHITECTURE OR OWNER APPROVAL
DDR.title: Provider adapter contract
DDR.description: Define a stable provider adapter interface with capability flags, normalized survey/status payloads, credential isolation, and certification tests.
DDR.source_excerpt: PROVIDER INTEGRATION FRAMEWORK / The platform must use a modular provider architecture. / Every provider should behave like a plugin. / Adding or removing a provider should require minimal changes. / The system should abstract provider-specific logic behind a common interface where feasible. / The platform should support independent provider configuration, health monitoring, logging, and error reporting. / Provider integrations must comply with each provider's published requirements and agreements. || Provider-specific logic should remain isolated behind integration layers where possible. || PROVIDER INTEGRATION LAYER / Create an abstraction layer for external providers. / The AI should design a provider interface that minimizes provider-specific code throughout the application. / When adding a new provider, implementation should primarily involve creating a new integration module rather than modifying core business logic. / Integrations should comply with each provider's published requirements and agreements.
DDR.decision_or_evidence_needed: Architecture approval and at least two provider proof-of-concept adapters.

DDR.label: DERIVED PROPOSAL — REQUIRES ARCHITECTURE OR OWNER APPROVAL
DDR.title: Webhook inbox and idempotency store
DDR.description: Persist verified webhook envelopes before processing, enforce provider/event idempotency keys, and retain retry/audit history.
DDR.source_excerpt: WEBHOOK ARCHITECTURE / Where supported by providers, design a secure webhook handling system. / Requirements include: / Verification of incoming requests / Logging / Retry handling / Idempotency / Error reporting / Monitoring / Webhook processing should be resilient and auditable.
DDR.decision_or_evidence_needed: Threat review, schema approval, replay policy, and provider verification tests.

DDR.label: DERIVED PROPOSAL — REQUIRES ARCHITECTURE OR OWNER APPROVAL
DDR.title: Policy engine for RBAC and Limit Templates
DDR.description: Centralize role permissions, account-state restrictions, and Limit Template overrides in one deny-by-default authorization policy evaluator.
DDR.source_excerpt: ACCOUNT MODERATION / Every account should support administrative states. / Examples include: / Active / Limited / Suspended / Disabled / Archived / The platform should be designed so additional states can be added later without requiring database redesign. / \--- / LIMIT TEMPLATE SYSTEM / Instead of manually configuring restrictions every time, create reusable Limit Templates. / Examples: / Template A / Withdrawal Restricted / Template B / Support Only / Template C / Read Only / Template D / Temporary Restriction / Template E / Survey Access Disabled / Each template should allow granular control over platform capabilities. / Examples of configurable permissions include: / Login / Profile Editing / Email Change / Password Change / Survey Access / Wallet Access / Withdrawal Access / Notifications / Blog Access / Referral Module (future) / Promotional Features (future) / Support Ticket Creation / Templates should be editable, cloneable, and assignable to users. / \--- / ROLE MANAGEMENT / The system should support multiple administrator roles. / Examples: / Super Admin / Operations Admin / Finance Admin / Support Admin / Content Admin / Marketing Admin / Developer / Read Only Auditor / Every role should use Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) with granular permissions. || The AI should ensure users can only access their own data unless explicitly authorized. || Administrative operations should require appropriate permissions.
DDR.decision_or_evidence_needed: Security architecture approval and policy-conflict test matrix.

DDR.label: DERIVED PROPOSAL — REQUIRES ARCHITECTURE OR OWNER APPROVAL
DDR.title: Versioned configuration registry
DDR.description: Store business settings as typed, versioned, effective-dated configuration with validation, change approval, rollback, and audit history.
DDR.source_excerpt: SYSTEM SETTINGS / Avoid hardcoding business values. / The following should be configurable from the admin panel whenever appropriate: / Points-to-USD conversion / Minimum withdrawal amount / Available withdrawal methods / Leaderboard settings / Registration controls / Email templates / Platform announcements / Maintenance mode / Feature flags / Currency display preferences / Country availability / Referral settings (future) / Reward campaigns (future) || CONFIGURATION PHILOSOPHY / Avoid hardcoded values whenever practical. / Business rules that are likely to change should be configurable through the Super Admin Panel. / Examples include: / Points conversion / Withdrawal thresholds / Feature availability / Country availability / Notification templates / Announcement banners / Maintenance mode / Reward campaigns / Leaderboard settings || BUSINESS RULE CONFIGURATION / Important business values must be configurable. / Examples: / 1000 Points \= 1 USD / Withdrawal threshold / Available countries / Reward rules / Feature availability / Leaderboard settings / Do not hardcode values that may change.
DDR.decision_or_evidence_needed: Architecture and owner approval of scope, rollout semantics, and emergency-change process.

DDR.label: DERIVED PROPOSAL — REQUIRES ARCHITECTURE OR OWNER APPROVAL
DDR.title: Tamper-evident audit log
DDR.description: Use append-only audit events with integrity chaining or equivalent tamper-evidence, protected access, export, and retention enforcement.
DDR.source_excerpt: AUDIT LOGGING / Every important administrative action should be logged. / Examples: / User modifications / Permission changes / Withdrawal approvals / Settings changes / Content updates / Login attempts / Failed authentication events / Audit logs should include: / Timestamp / Administrator / Action / Target / Reason (where applicable) / IP information if appropriate / Outcome / Audit records should be searchable. || Audit Domain / Maintain immutable records of significant administrative and system actions. / Examples include: / Settings changes / User moderation / Permission changes / Administrative actions

DDR.label: DERIVED PROPOSAL — REQUIRES ARCHITECTURE OR OWNER APPROVAL
DDR.title: Transactional outbox and resilient job processing
DDR.description: Use a transactional outbox for state-change notifications and jobs, plus retries, backoff, dead-letter handling, deduplication, and operator replay.
DDR.source_excerpt: BACKGROUND PROCESSING / Long-running or scheduled tasks should be separated from the main user request flow where appropriate. / Examples: / Email sending / Notification processing / Scheduled synchronization / Data cleanup / Report generation / Maintenance routines / The AI should recommend the most suitable architecture for these workloads based on the selected infrastructure. || BACKGROUND PROCESSING / Long-running API operations should be processed asynchronously where appropriate. / Examples include: / Email delivery / Notification delivery / Synchronization / Scheduled maintenance / Reporting / The AI should recommend the most suitable job processing approach based on the selected infrastructure. || BACKGROUND JOB ARCHITECTURE / The platform will require background processing. / Examples: / Email sending / Survey synchronization / Reward updates / Notification processing / Analytics processing / Scheduled tasks / The AI should design a reliable job system. / Requirements: / Retry handling / Failure tracking / Monitoring / Queue management
DDR.decision_or_evidence_needed: Architecture approval and failure/recovery test evidence.

DDR.label: DERIVED PROPOSAL — REQUIRES ARCHITECTURE OR OWNER APPROVAL
DDR.title: Contract-first API specification
DDR.description: Use a versioned OpenAPI contract as the single API documentation/test-generation source with standard envelopes and error schemas.
DDR.source_excerpt: API DESIGN PRINCIPLES / Every API should follow consistent standards. / Examples include: / Consistent naming conventions / Standard request validation / Standard response structure / Meaningful error messages / Pagination for large datasets / Filtering / Sorting / Search / Versioning / Rate limiting where appropriate / The AI should recommend and document these standards before implementation. || API DOCUMENTATION / Generate comprehensive API documentation. / Include: / Authentication flow / Endpoint descriptions / Request examples / Response examples / Error documentation / Version history / Integration guidance / Documentation should remain synchronized with implementation. || FINAL API DELIVERABLES / Before implementation, generate: / 1\. API Architecture Document / 2\. Authentication Flow Documentation / 3\. API Standards Guide / 4\. Provider Integration Guide / 5\. Webhook Design Guide / 6\. Error Handling Standards / 7\. Security Review / 8\. Testing Strategy / 9\. API Documentation / 10\. Implementation Roadmap
DDR.decision_or_evidence_needed: API architecture approval and CI contract-drift enforcement proof.

DDR.label: DERIVED PROPOSAL — REQUIRES ARCHITECTURE OR OWNER APPROVAL
DDR.title: Modular-monolith initial topology
DDR.description: Begin with a modular monolith whose domain boundaries can be extracted later, avoiding premature distributed-system complexity while preserving API contracts.
DDR.source_excerpt: ENGINEERING PRINCIPLES / The platform must be: / Modular / Loosely coupled / Highly cohesive / API-friendly / Cloud-ready / Mobile-ready / Future-proof / Easily testable / Well documented / Version controlled / Avoid unnecessary complexity. / \--- / PROJECT STRUCTURE / The AI should organize the project using a clean architecture. / Suggested high-level modules include: / Authentication / User Management / Wallet / Rewards / Surveys / Withdrawals / Notifications / CMS / Blog / Support / Leaderboards / Admin ERP / Analytics / Settings / Audit Logs / Background Jobs / Integrations / Each module should have clear boundaries and minimal coupling. || EarnPearls must be designed with a startup-friendly but enterprise-ready infrastructure approach. / The platform should begin with cost-efficient infrastructure while maintaining a clear migration path toward larger enterprise infrastructure as user growth increases. / The architecture must avoid vendor lock-in wherever practical. || FINAL INFRASTRUCTURE DIRECTIVE / Build EarnPearls like a serious global platform, but respect startup realities. / Do not over-engineer too early. / Do not create a fragile prototype. / Create a foundation that can start cheaply and grow professionally.
DDR.decision_or_evidence_needed: Backend architecture comparison and explicit owner approval.

DDR.label: DERIVED PROPOSAL — REQUIRES ARCHITECTURE OR OWNER APPROVAL
DDR.title: Unified observability correlation
DDR.description: Propagate correlation IDs across requests, jobs, provider calls, audit events, and financial transactions, with structured logs, metrics, traces, and alerts.
DDR.source_excerpt: OBSERVABILITY / Design the API layer to support operational visibility. / Consider: / Structured logging / Metrics / Request tracing / Health checks / Error monitoring / Performance monitoring / The AI should recommend tools and architecture appropriate for the chosen technology stack. || MONITORING & OBSERVABILITY / The platform should monitor: / Application Health / Errors / Response times / Failed requests / Infrastructure / CPU / Memory / Storage / Database performance / Business Metrics / Signups / Survey activity / Withdrawals / Revenue / \--- / LOGGING STRATEGY / Implement structured logging. / Logs should help investigate: / Errors / Security events / User actions / Integration failures / Avoid storing unnecessary sensitive information.
DDR.decision_or_evidence_needed: Observability design approval, privacy review, and incident drill.

DDR.label: DERIVED PROPOSAL — REQUIRES ARCHITECTURE OR OWNER APPROVAL
DDR.title: Retention and erasure policy engine
DDR.description: Implement category-based retention, legal hold, anonymization, deletion jobs, and evidence reports from an approved policy table.
DDR.source_excerpt: DATA RETENTION / The AI should recommend retention policies for different categories of data. / Examples: / Logs / Audit records / Notifications / Sessions / Support tickets / The recommendations should balance operational needs, storage costs, and applicable legal obligations. || Avoid storing unnecessary sensitive information.
DDR.decision_or_evidence_needed: Legal/owner approval and end-to-end deletion/hold tests.

DDR.label: DERIVED PROPOSAL — REQUIRES ARCHITECTURE OR OWNER APPROVAL
DDR.title: FX-rate snapshot service
DDR.description: Store the source, timestamp, rate, base currency, quote currency, and rounding policy used for each displayed local-currency estimate.
DDR.source_excerpt: Users should see: / Points / USD / Estimated Local Currency / Local currency is display-only. / All calculations, accounting, wallet balances, provider earnings, and business reporting must use USD as the source of truth. || Every page should display: / Points / USD / Estimated Local Currency
DDR.decision_or_evidence_needed: Finance/owner approval and source reliability evidence.

DDR.label: DERIVED PROPOSAL — REQUIRES ARCHITECTURE OR OWNER APPROVAL
DDR.title: Idempotent withdrawal orchestration
DDR.description: Use an idempotency key, reservation/hold posting, provider attempt log, reconciliation state, and safe retry rules for each withdrawal.
DDR.source_excerpt: WITHDRAWAL SYSTEM / The withdrawal experience should feel professional and transparent. / Supported withdrawal methods should be designed to support: / PayPal / Virtual Visa / Cryptocurrency / The system architecture should make it easy to add additional methods later. / Each withdrawal should display: / Request Date / Processing Status / Estimated Completion / Completed Date / Transaction Reference / Support Link / Every withdrawal should generate a unique transaction ID. || Withdrawal Domain / Track: / Requests / Status / Amount / Points / Currency / Payment method / Processing timestamps / References / Administrative actions / The history should be immutable wherever practical. || WITHDRAWAL APIs / Support: / Available Methods / Withdrawal Request / Withdrawal Status / Withdrawal History / Validation / The system should validate requests before processing.
DDR.decision_or_evidence_needed: Finance/security architecture approval and duplicate-payment prevention tests.

EFE.label: EFE
EFE.title: Provider contracts and integration specifications
EFE.description: Current provider agreements, API/webhook documentation, status semantics, validation evidence, settlement terms, reversals, country/device rules, and data-use limits must be verified.
EFE.source_excerpt: Survey Providers (without misleading claims) || SURVEY EXPERIENCE / Survey discovery must be extremely simple. / Users should instantly understand: / Reward / Estimated Time / Difficulty (if available) / Availability / Category / Country Eligibility / Device Compatibility / When a survey is clicked: / Open according to provider integration requirements. / Do not modify provider workflows in ways that violate provider agreements. / After completion: / Automatically synchronize status if supported. / If immediate confirmation is unavailable, clearly explain that validation may take time depending on the provider. || PROVIDER INTEGRATION FRAMEWORK / The platform must use a modular provider architecture. / Every provider should behave like a plugin. / Adding or removing a provider should require minimal changes. / The system should abstract provider-specific logic behind a common interface where feasible. / The platform should support independent provider configuration, health monitoring, logging, and error reporting. / Provider integrations must comply with each provider's published requirements and agreements. || PROVIDER INTEGRATION LAYER / Create an abstraction layer for external providers. / The AI should design a provider interface that minimizes provider-specific code throughout the application. / When adding a new provider, implementation should primarily involve creating a new integration module rather than modifying core business logic. / Integrations should comply with each provider's published requirements and agreements. / \--- / WEBHOOK ARCHITECTURE / Where supported by providers, design a secure webhook handling system. / Requirements include: / Verification of incoming requests / Logging / Retry handling / Idempotency / Error reporting / Monitoring / Webhook processing should be resilient and auditable.
EFE.decision_or_evidence_needed: Provider-issued current contracts and technical documentation, retained with version/date and approval record.

EFE.label: EFE
EFE.title: Withdrawal-provider availability and terms
EFE.description: Country availability, currencies, fees, settlement, reserves, transaction limits, API capability, dispute handling, and prohibited use for PayPal, Virtual Visa, crypto, or alternatives require current evidence.
EFE.source_excerpt: Supported withdrawal methods should be designed to support: / PayPal / Virtual Visa / Cryptocurrency / The system architecture should make it easy to add additional methods later. || WITHDRAWAL APIs / Support: / Available Methods / Withdrawal Request / Withdrawal Status / Withdrawal History / Validation / The system should validate requests before processing.
EFE.decision_or_evidence_needed: Official provider documentation and signed commercial/compliance terms.

EFE.label: EFE
EFE.title: Target-market legal and privacy obligations
EFE.description: Privacy, cookies, consumer disclosures, promotions, age/consent, marketing communications, data rights, retention, taxation, and rewards-platform rules vary by launch market.
EFE.source_excerpt: TARGET COUNTRIES / Primary launch markets include: / United States / United Kingdom / Canada / Ireland / Australia / Germany / Belgium / Other selected European countries / Saudi Arabia / United Arab Emirates / Qatar / Oman / Bahrain / The initial public launch should not target Pakistan, India, Bangladesh, or China. / The platform architecture should still be capable of supporting additional countries in the future if the business expands. || Only collect data that is necessary for the platform. || DATA RETENTION / The AI should recommend retention policies for different categories of data. / Examples: / Logs / Audit records / Notifications / Sessions / Support tickets / The recommendations should balance operational needs, storage costs, and applicable legal obligations. || TARGET AUDIENCE / Primary audiences: / United States / United Kingdom / Canada / Australia / Ireland / Germany / Selected European Markets / GCC Countries: / Saudi Arabia / UAE / Qatar / Oman / Bahrain / Marketing campaigns should be adapted based on: / Country / Culture / Language behavior / Internet habits / Reward preferences
EFE.decision_or_evidence_needed: Qualified legal analysis by jurisdiction with dated sources and applicability matrix.

EFE.label: EFE
EFE.title: Cloud and managed-service pricing/limits
EFE.description: Free tiers, quotas, pricing, SLA, region availability, lock-in, migration tools, and service limits are time-sensitive external facts.
EFE.source_excerpt: INFRASTRUCTURE STRATEGY / The AI must evaluate available infrastructure options objectively. / Do not select technology based only on popularity. / Evaluate based on: / Free-tier availability / Resource limits / Scalability / Reliability / Security / Developer experience / Documentation quality / Long-term cost / Migration difficulty / \--- / FREE-FIRST APPROACH / During the initial startup phase, prioritize free or extremely low-cost solutions where practical. / The AI should analyze options such as: / AWS Free Tier / AWS Lambda / Cloudflare Workers / Cloudflare Pages / Google Cloud Free Tier / Google Apps Script (where appropriate) / Supabase / Neon PostgreSQL / Managed MySQL/MariaDB solutions / Other suitable startup platforms / The AI must recommend the best combination with reasoning. / Do not choose free services if they create future technical debt. || DATABASE INFRASTRUCTURE / The AI should evaluate: / PostgreSQL / MySQL / MariaDB / Serverless databases / Managed database services / Consider: / Free tier limits / Backups / Performance / Scaling options / Security / Migration possibilities / The database must not become the first bottleneck. / \--- / STORAGE ARCHITECTURE / Define storage strategy for: / User uploads / Blog images / Documents / System files / Backups / The AI should consider: / Object storage / CDN integration / Cost optimization
EFE.decision_or_evidence_needed: Current official vendor documentation and dated cost/limit comparison.

EFE.label: EFE
EFE.title: Email deliverability and provider terms
EFE.description: Free limits, deliverability, API quality, sending-domain requirements, suppression handling, regional availability, and marketing restrictions require verification.
EFE.source_excerpt: EMAIL SYSTEM / Support transactional emails for: / Email verification / Password reset / Security notifications / Withdrawal updates / Platform announcements / Support ticket updates / The AI should evaluate and recommend the most suitable email delivery solution based on reliability, scalability, cost, and free-tier availability. || EMAIL INFRASTRUCTURE / The system requires reliable email delivery. / Evaluate providers based on: / Free limits / Deliverability / API quality / Reliability / Scalability / Use email infrastructure for: / Account verification / Password reset / Security notifications / Withdrawal notifications / Support updates / Marketing communication (future)
EFE.decision_or_evidence_needed: Official provider documentation, current pricing, deliverability test, and acceptable-use review.

EFE.label: EFE
EFE.title: SMS/OTP provider coverage and regulation
EFE.description: SMS coverage, sender registration, cost, delivery, fraud controls, privacy terms, and verification-service availability vary by country.
EFE.source_excerpt: Phone verification is not required during registration. / Phone OTP verification should occur only when required for sensitive actions (such as the first withdrawal), if the business chooses to enable it. || OTP INFRASTRUCTURE / OTP requirements: / Secure generation / Expiration / Rate limiting / Abuse prevention / Logging / The AI should recommend: / Email OTP / SMS OTP / Third-party verification services / based on: / Cost / Reliability / Target countries
EFE.decision_or_evidence_needed: Official provider coverage/pricing plus country-specific messaging and consent review.

EFE.label: EFE
EFE.title: Foreign-exchange data source
EFE.description: Accuracy, licensing, update frequency, outage policy, and attribution requirements of the chosen FX source require current evidence.
EFE.source_excerpt: Users should see: / Points / USD / Estimated Local Currency / Local currency is display-only. / All calculations, accounting, wallet balances, provider earnings, and business reporting must use USD as the source of truth. || Every page should display: / Points / USD / Estimated Local Currency
EFE.decision_or_evidence_needed: Official data-provider terms, SLA/limits, accuracy test, and finance approval.

EFE.label: EFE
EFE.title: Accessibility conformance baseline
EFE.description: The Constitution requires accessibility best practices but does not name a conformance standard or level.
EFE.source_excerpt: ACCESSIBILITY / Design for broad usability. / Include: / Keyboard navigation / Proper labels / Logical focus order / Adequate color contrast / Screen reader support where practical / Accessibility should be part of the initial design. || DESIGN ACCESSIBILITY / Follow accessibility best practices. / Support: / Keyboard navigation / Visible focus states / Readable contrast / Scalable text / Screen reader compatibility where practical / Avoid relying solely on color to communicate meaning.
EFE.decision_or_evidence_needed: Current authoritative accessibility standard, approved conformance level, and legal applicability review.

EFE.label: EFE
EFE.title: Core Web Vitals thresholds
EFE.description: “Excellent Core Web Vitals” requires current metric definitions and threshold evidence.
EFE.source_excerpt: PERFORMANCE TARGETS / The platform should aim for: / Fast initial page load / Optimized images / Lazy loading / Efficient caching / Minimal JavaScript / Excellent Core Web Vitals / Responsive mobile experience / The AI should recommend measurable performance targets and architecture choices to support them.
EFE.decision_or_evidence_needed: Current official web performance definitions, field-measurement method, and approved budgets.

EFE.label: EFE
EFE.title: Payments, crypto, KYC, AML, and sanctions applicability
EFE.description: Withdrawal methods and target countries may trigger identity, payments, virtual-asset, sanctions, tax, or AML obligations.
EFE.source_excerpt: Supported withdrawal methods should be designed to support: / PayPal / Virtual Visa / Cryptocurrency / The system architecture should make it easy to add additional methods later. || SECURITY PRINCIPLE / Security is not an optional feature. / It must exist from the beginning. / Always consider: / User privacy / Financial data protection / Account security / Fraud prevention / Abuse prevention / Secure integrations
EFE.decision_or_evidence_needed: Qualified legal/compliance opinion and provider-specific onboarding requirements.

EFE.label: EFE
EFE.title: Data residency, backup, and cross-border transfer constraints
EFE.description: Hosting regions, storage, logs, backups, disaster recovery, and cross-border transfers may be constrained by target-market law and vendor terms.
EFE.source_excerpt: CLOUD ARCHITECTURE REQUIREMENTS / The system should be designed with separation between: / Frontend / Backend Services / Database / Storage / Email Delivery / Background Jobs / Monitoring / Third-party Integrations / This allows individual components to scale independently. || BACKUP STRATEGY / Create a complete backup plan. / Include: / Database backups / File backups / Configuration backups / Define: / Backup frequency / Storage location / Recovery process / Testing procedure / \--- / DISASTER RECOVERY / Create a recovery strategy. / Define: / Recovery Time Objective (RTO) / Recovery Point Objective (RPO) / Emergency procedures / Responsible roles
EFE.decision_or_evidence_needed: Legal applicability matrix plus official vendor region, encryption, replication, and transfer documentation.

EFE.label: EFE
EFE.title: Current application-security standards and threat data
EFE.description: Security controls, abuse limits, dependency risks, and secure-development practices require current authoritative baselines.
EFE.source_excerpt: SECURITY / Security is a core requirement. / The AI must propose a comprehensive security architecture that includes: / Secure authentication / Session management / CSRF protection / XSS protection / SQL injection prevention / Secure password hashing / Rate limiting / Brute-force protection / Input validation / Output encoding / Secure file handling / Secure API design / Security headers / Logging and monitoring / Backup strategy / Disaster recovery planning / The AI should justify major security decisions. || API SECURITY / The API architecture should include recommendations for: / Authentication / Authorization / Rate limiting / Input validation / Output encoding / Request logging / Abuse detection / Session security / Secret management / Security should be considered throughout the design rather than added afterward. || SECURITY OPERATIONS / Infrastructure security must include: / Secret management / Access control / Firewall rules where applicable / Secure environment variables / Dependency monitoring / Regular updates
EFE.decision_or_evidence_needed: Current authoritative security standards, threat model, dependency advisories, and control mapping.

OCR.label: OCR
OCR.title: Pending-to-Validated is event-driven
OCR.description: Pending → Validated requires provider confirmation or verified reconciliation. Elapsed time alone never validates a provider transaction.
OCR.source_excerpt: No Constitution wording is claimed for this gap.
OCR.decision_or_evidence_needed: Implement as a binding owner rule after independent review.
OCR.notes: Constitution L669–L693 defines the lifecycle sequence only; it does not state this trigger. No Constitution citation is fabricated.

OCR.label: OCR
OCR.title: No global maturity or hold period
OCR.description: Validated → Mature may depend on provider-specific settlement and risk rules; Mature → Withdrawable requires cleared-funds confirmation and configured risk conditions. No single global hold period is assumed.
OCR.source_excerpt: No Constitution wording is claimed for this gap.
OCR.notes: This is a binding owner clarification recorded outside the Constitution and is excluded from the formal REQ total.

OCR.label: OCR
OCR.title: Canonical citation discipline
OCR.description: Every Constitution citation uses verified exact canonical line ranges, with each non-contiguous range recorded separately.
OCR.source_excerpt: No Constitution wording is claimed for this gap.
OCR.decision_or_evidence_needed: Apply to every register revision and independent review.
OCR.notes: This is a remediation governance rule, not a product requirement and not Constitution wording.
